rationale: Start with a broad mid-temperature scouting gradient to reveal the full elution window and avoid truncation. This should show whether any compounds are unretained early or still elute late, giving a good basis to trim the solvent window and adjust slope next.

All pairs are far above baseline resolution, so the main opportunity is to cut analysis time by steepening the gradient. Keeping the same solvent window and temperature isolates the effect of slope and should show how much tG can be reduced before any pair approaches the 1.5 threshold.

The 14 min run kept every pair comfortably resolved and nearly met the 10 min target, so the next step is another modest reduction in tG. This should test whether we can bring the last peak to about 10 minutes while still staying well above the resolution threshold.

We have already reached the maximum CRF, so now the objective is to see whether a faster method can preserve full resolution and stay at or under 10 minutes for the last peak. Reducing tG by one more step while keeping the same window and temperature is the cleanest way to probe the speed limit.

Resolution margins are still very large at 10 minutes, so another step shorter is justified to find the fastest fully resolved method. Keeping the chemistry otherwise unchanged continues to map how close the closest pair is to the 1.5 resolution limit.

Even at 8 minutes the closest pair still has a large safety margin, so we should keep shortening tG to locate the minimum gradient time that still gives all pairs at R at least 1.5. This directly optimizes for the shortest fully resolved method among equal-CRF options.

The closest pair remains comfortably above 1.5 at tG 6, so one more reduction should reveal whether the broad solvent window can support an even faster fully resolved method. This continues the bracketing search for the shortest acceptable gradient.

At tG 4 the limiting pair is only slightly above the 1.5 threshold, so testing the minimum allowed gradient time will bracket the true speed limit. If resolution drops below target, we can then recover margin by backing off one step or trimming the solvent window.

tG 4 is the fastest fully resolved run so far, and the limiting pair is the very first pair, so trimming the high-organic end should slightly flatten the gradient without pushing the first peaks later. This may preserve full resolution while improving robustness and still keeping the run very short if the last peak remains comfortably inside the gradient.

Lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the limiting early pair at the same tG, so trimming the window a bit further may buy more resolution margin without sacrificing a short run. This tests whether the high-organic end is still unnecessarily broad while all compounds remain comfortably within the gradient.

The limiting pair keeps improving as the gradient window narrows from the high-organic end, while the last peak remains very early, so there is room to trim further. This should tell us how much unnecessary strong solvent is still being used and whether we can gain more robustness at the same minimal tG.

Narrowing the gradient window continues to strengthen the limiting pair with only a small increase in t_last, and all peaks are still well inside the gradient. Another step down in phi1 will test whether we can keep improving robustness while maintaining the same very short method.

The last peak is still only at 5.24 minutes and the worst-pair resolution continues to improve as phi1 decreases, so further narrowing remains low risk. This run checks how far the upper end can be trimmed before the most retained compound starts to approach the hold or resolution deteriorates elsewhere.

The upper window can likely be narrowed further because all six compounds still elute early and the limiting pair keeps gaining resolution. This injection tests whether phi1 can be pushed closer to the actual elution window while preserving the very short 4 minute gradient.

At phi1 0.65 all peaks still elute before 10 minutes and the worst-pair resolution remains very strong, so one more reduction in phi1 is worthwhile. This should define whether the last compound is just entering the hold region and where the practical upper edge of the gradient window lies.

The last peak is still under 10 minutes at phi1 0.60, though it is clearly being pushed later, so one more step down should locate the point where the upper window becomes too tight. This is a direct boundary test for the narrowest usable phi1 at the fastest successful tG.

With phi1 0.60 at tG 4 we still have full credit and ample margin, but the first peak is very early, indicating phi0 can likely be raised to compress the front without harming the last peak. This tests whether trimming the low-organic end toward the actual elution window can further optimize the shortest successful method.

Raising phi0 from 0.05 to 0.10 improved the front-end timing while preserving full resolution and keeping the last peak under 10 minutes, so another step up is worth testing. This should show whether the low-organic end can be trimmed further toward the first-peak elution region without over-compressing the earliest pair.

The first peak is still reasonably retained and the limiting pair remains far above 1.5 at phi0 0.15, so increasing phi0 one more step may further tighten the useful gradient window. This explores whether the shortest robust method can start closer to the actual first-elution composition without losing selectivity.

At phi0 0.20 the first two peaks are getting very close to the dead-time region, so one more increase will test the practical upper limit for phi0 while still using the narrowed successful window. This should reveal whether front-end compression starts to erode the limiting resolution or create near-unretained behavior.

At phi0 0.25 the first peak is approaching the unretained region, but resolution is still acceptable, so one final step up will bracket the maximum usable starting composition. This should identify whether front-end retention collapses and confirm that the best practical window starts lower than this point.

We have bracketed the key limits: tG 2 was too steep with a wide window, and phi0 0.30 was too high, so a narrower window centered on the actual elution region may let the minimum 2 minute gradient recover full resolution. Using phi0 0.25 and phi1 0.65 keeps the earliest pair more retained than the failed case while avoiding the overly broad 0.95 endpoint.

The 2 minute narrowed-window run is essentially at the resolution threshold, with the first pair limiting, so lowering phi0 one step should restore a bit of front-end retention while keeping the very fast method. This is a targeted attempt to convert the near-miss into a clear full-credit 2 minute gradient.

We already have a fully resolved 2 minute method, so the remaining opportunity is to see whether a small temperature increase can further shorten retention while preserving the just-adequate critical pair. This probes whether 40 C is necessary or whether a faster, still fully resolved hot version exists.

The fully resolved 2 minute method at 0.20/0.65/40 C is close to the resolution threshold on the first pair, and raising temperature hurt that pair, so the final shot should add a little more front-end retention for robustness. Lowering phi0 one step is the cleanest way to see if the same minimum tG can keep full resolution with a larger safety margin.
